headline: Higher metal prices drive a sharp profit jump, output slips

kpis.label: Operating cash cost before by-product credits
Operating cash cost net of by-product credits

summary_short: Southern Copper's Q2 2026 net sales rose 40.6% y/y to $4,289.0M and net income attributable to SCC jumped 71.6% to $1,670.0M ($2.01 diluted EPS), as higher copper, molybdenum and silver prices more than offset a 3.5% drop in copper mine production.
summary_long: Revenue growth (+40.6% y/y) was driven entirely by price: LME copper +39.8%, molybdenum +43.1%, silver +118.6%, zinc +30.8%, even as sales volumes fell across all four metals. Copper mine production fell 3.5% y/y on lower ore grades at Toquepala (-14.7%) and Cuajone (-7.8%), partly offset by Buenavista, La Caridad and IMMSA. Operating cash cost before by-product credits rose to $2.29/lb (+8.3%); net of credits it improved to $0.05/lb from $0.63/lb on stronger molybdenum and silver by-products. Operating costs grew only 13.8% against 40.6% revenue growth, expanding margins. Cash rose to $5,665.0M; capex rose 79.4% to $422.8M. The Board declared a Q3 dividend of $1.10 cash plus a stock dividend (~$3.23/share combined) on July 16, 2026.

drivers.explanation: Higher metal prices (LME copper +39.8%, molybdenum +43.1%, silver +118.6%, zinc +30.8%) drove the increase despite lower sales volumes across all four metals.
Higher net sales (+40.6%) reflecting higher metal prices, while operating costs increased at a considerably lower rate (+13.8%).
Lower production at Toquepala (-14.7%, lower ore grades and mineral milled) and Cuajone (-7.8%, lower ore grades), partly offset by Buenavista, La Caridad and IMMSA gains.

drivers.metric: Operating cash cost before by-product credits
drivers.explanation: Unit-cost effect of lower copper production plus higher fuel and operating-material costs, partly offset by lower treatment and refining charges.

drivers.metric: Operating cash cost net of by-product credits
drivers.explanation: By-product revenue per pound rose 51.4% (to $2.24 from $1.48) on higher molybdenum and silver prices, more than offsetting the rise in cost before credits.
Revenue growth outpaced cost growth (+40.6% vs +13.8%), expanding margins and driving the profit and cash-flow beat.
